cards.title: Managing Enterprise VR Fleets as Meta's Offer Changes
cards.angle: Meta ended commercial Quest sales and new Horizon Managed Services subscriptions on February 20 2026; existing customers keep support to January 4 2030. The clock on provisioning, kiosk lockdown and remote wipe is now visible.
cards.evidence: Your Woolworths deployment runs 2,000 headsets across 1,000+ stores on Strivr, the largest fleet of its kind in Australian retail. No piece on your site tells a retail IT lead what the next four years of fleet management look like.

cards.title: 360 Video or Real-Time 3D for Accredited Training
cards.angle: World Labs opened a World API in January 2026 that generates navigable 3D scenes from text or panoramas. Accredited units still need actor realism, a tablet fallback and an auditor who accepts the scenario, and generative 3D has none of that yet.
cards.evidence: Your Limestone Coast build delivers ASQA-compliant aged care and disability units on live-action 360 with branching, one facilitator to 28 learners on headsets and iPads. The tradeoff piece (reshoot cost versus assessment validity) is one only a studio that has shipped both can write.

cards.title: Confidence Is Not Competence Under the Aged Care Act
cards.angle: The new Aged Care Act commenced November 1 2025 and providers now report training against it. Self-reported confidence is the easiest outcome to collect and the weakest one to defend.
cards.evidence: Sacadi VR launched in February 2026 for aged care compliance, and your strongest published outcome is Reject Shop's "very confident" rising from 18 to 68 percent (n=95), explicitly a participant confidence measure. The article maps the ladder from confidence to observed competence and what each rung costs.
